next_round_constraints: Keep search focused on SEIRS with fractional=1 and observation_map=delayed_I; explore delay_weeks in a narrow neighborhood around the best-performing delays (1–3) rather than expanding broadly.
Include a small comparator set of SEIHR with observation_map=H only (avoid I+H mapping given poor performance) to test whether explicit hospitalization state improves stability across rolling splits.
Prioritize templates expected to be robust to peak timing (high peakiness) and avoid adding extra complexity beyond what is needed to resolve delay vs. hospitalization-state ambiguity.
Do not introduce new observation maps beyond delayed_I (for SEIRS) and H (for SEIHR) in the next round; keep the candidate set tight to improve identifiability.
observed_failure_modes: Delay sensitivity: delayed_I with 1–3 week delays yields similar rolling behavior but noticeably different validation fit, suggesting the observation delay is not well-identified and may be compensating for other dynamics.
Generalization gap: some specs show better single validation fit than rolling averages, indicating potential overfitting to the specific validation window timing/phase rather than stable dynamics.

Structure mismatch risk: SEIHR with direct H observation is competitive but not clearly superior, implying hospitalization dynamics may be partially captured by delayed incidence rather than an explicit H compartment; mapping choice remains ambiguous.
Instability under splits: non-trivial rolling std MAE across candidates suggests parameter/phase sensitivity (peak timing/height) for this high/peaky series.
feedback.proposer_instruction: For next round proposals on the >=65 hospitalization-rate series: (1) concentrate on SEIRS fractional with delayed_I and test delay_weeks = {1,2,3} with minor variations only (no new maps/extra compartments); aim for improved rolling-split consistency rather than optimizing a single window. (2) Add a limited SEIHR baseline using observation_map=H (no I+H) to check whether an explicit H state reduces split sensitivity. Keep complexity minimal and focus on resolving whether delay-only observation or explicit hospitalization compartment better captures peak timing/shape.
